overview: White develops the bishop to d3 before the knights, avoiding the main French tabiyas, but the bishop blocks the d-pawn and Black can strike at once. Black typically replies 3...c5, 3...dxe4 4.Bxe4 Nf6 or 3...Nf6 and equalises easily. I am not sure of the theory, but the line is a rarely chosen sideline that offers White little.

white_ideas.idea: Develop quickly with Bd3, Ne2 or Nf3 and castle, keeping the centre intact.
Meet ...c5 with dxc5 or c3 and aim at a kingside attack with the bishop on d3.

black_ideas.idea: Strike at the centre with ...c5 or ...dxe4 followed by ...Nf6 and ...c5.
Equalise by exchanging in the centre and developing the light bishop.

typical_structures.structure: French pawn centre e4/d4 against e6/d5 with an early ...c5 strike.

character.notes: Black's solid French structure and the quiet exchange lines give steady play.

soundness.notes: Sound but gives Black an easy game.

structure.notes: French centre with tension on d4 and e4 left unresolved.

approach.notes: Rare sideline, not chosen by strong players much.

level.notes: Easy ideas but not worth building on.

character.reason: Black's French structure is hard to break down and White plays quietly.

structure.reason: Centre tension unresolved at the root.

level.reason: Simple ideas but not a first repertoire choice.
